gaps.sentence: She got ___ injury during the warm-up.
gaps.explanation: 'An injury' — vowel sound; 'during the warm-up' is the specific one.

gaps.sentence: My uncle is ___ university lecturer and a painter in his free time.
gaps.explanation: 'A university lecturer' (the u sounds like /juː/); the second gap is also 'an artist'.

gaps.sentence: ___ bicycles are a cheap way of seeing the city.
gaps.explanation: Plural nouns in a general sense take no article.

gaps.sentence: ___ honest answer would have saved everyone time.
We stayed at ___ hotel right next to the station.
gaps.explanation: 'The station' — in a town there is usually one known station; context makes it definite.

gaps.sentence: ___ weather was so bad that the match was abandoned.
gaps.explanation: The weather is always definite in a situation.

gaps.sentence: It's ___ one-way street, so you can't turn left here.
gaps.explanation: 'One' starts with /w/, a consonant sound, so 'a one-way street'.

gaps.sentence: ___ good news is that sales are up by twenty per cent.
gaps.explanation: 'News' is uncountable but takes 'the' when specified: the good news is… 'Sales' here is general, so no article.
